thesis: Gamuda has a genuinely improving construction engine, but 29.35x trailing earnings prices more progress than the observed 5% group profit growth. The bear wins on the scale of financing dependence: 72% gearing and RM3.401bn investing outflow against RM807.6m CFO. A profitable RM61.2bn backlog and construction profit growth preserve credible upside, preventing financing risk alone from proving a sell.
strongest_counterexample: Construction profit rose 19% at a stable 5% segment margin, and CFO improved from negative RM78.5m to positive RM807.6m; this is delivered operating progress rather than merely a backlog promise.
invalidation_conditions: Observed net gearing below the management-stated 70% objective by late FY27, with CFO exceeding the FY26 RM807.6m baseline, would weaken the financing-restraint ruling.
Construction segment net margin below the observed 5.0% and a return to negative annual CFO would invalidate the preserved execution-upside counterweight.
decisive_factors: Gearing rose from 53% to 72%; short-term borrowings rose to RM6.341bn.
Positive CFO does not fund the current investment scale; investing outflow is not mislabeled recurring capex.
